call_chain_analysis: The finding ID 383d4bbee0 = sha1('proofhound.js.redos|lib/static.js|55|16')[:10] (verified; src/proofhound/core/analysis/semgrep.py:124). The sink at lib/static.js:55 col 16 is the `purl` argument of `/\/$/.test(purl)`. Taint chain: `exports.writeStatic` (lib/static.js:3) is the module entry point. It computes `url = request.url.replace(/[?#][\s\S]*/,'')` at line 9, then `filepath = Path.join(root, url)` at line 10. Root is `require.resolve('api-proxy/lib/static.js'), '../../www'` which resolves to the api-proxy package's own www/ directory. It calls `FS.stat(filepath, cb)` (line 14); the callback only enters the writeDir branch when `stats.isDirectory()` is true (line 15), i.e. only when `filepath` already exists on disk as a directory. writeDir (line 52) re-reads `request.url` (not the sanitised `url` from writeStatic), computes `purl = url.replace(/[?].*$/,'')` (line 54), and tests it with `/\/$/.test(purl)` (line 55). The fuzz-controlled byte here is the whole request.url minus any trailing `?...` suffix; its length and character set are otherwise unconstrained.
argument_reasoning: The 'catastrophic input' the task asks for cannot exist for this regex. `/\/$/` is a two-char anchored pattern (literal `/` followed by `$`). It compiles to one state that peeks at the last character of the subject string; it has zero alternations, zero repetitions, zero branches, so it exposes no backtracking surface at all. Running it on `'a'^N` (any N) is O(1) in V8 — the engine inspects the final byte of the UTF-16 buffer and returns false. The preceding `url.replace(/[?].*$/,'')` is also linear (greedy `.*` anchored to `$`). We still built the strongest-possible probe for completeness: a 1 MiB string of fuzz-controlled bytes with no trailing `/`, repeated so the regex engine must scan the whole buffer. At -timeout=2 with --sync the harness averaged ~430 execs/s and completed 13 453 runs with no timeout, confirming the sink runs in low microseconds per call. The SAST rule flagged this as a *candidate* (its own comment: 'The regex's own complexity is confirmed dynamically ... so this flags a candidate, not a proven ReDoS'); for finding 383d4bbee0 the dynamic confirmation is negative. This is a true SAST false positive: tainted data does reach a RegExp, but the regex is not vulnerable.

lessons:
1. The sink `/\/$/.test(purl)` is a true SAST false positive for ReDoS. The semgrep rule proofhound.js.redos only verifies that tainted data reaches a RegExp — it does not analyse the regex's complexity. A one-character end-anchored class (no alternation, no repetition) has no backtracking surface and will never ReDoS, no matter the payload. A 7B model that learns to produce a harness for 383d4bbee0 will be learning to confirm a bug that is not there. For distillation it is still useful signal, but as a negative example: the right output here is `attempts_before_success: null` with the regex-shape explanation, not a confirmed-crash trajectory.

2. The current Jazzer.js adapter (src/proofhound/core/adapters/javascript.py) treats `ERROR: libFuzzer: timeout` as kind='Timeout' with is_vulnerability=False, and kind_matches_class('Timeout', 'redos') is False (core/models.py). So even for a genuinely catastrophic regex, the pipeline cannot record crash_confirmed=True today. Any work aimed at pushing ReDoS confirmation rate above 0/57 in v4 must first add 'Timeout' (or an equivalent slow-regex kind) to SECURITY_DETECTORS and teach kind_matches_class to map it to 'redos'. Without that, every ReDoS trajectory will be partial.

3. Reaching the sink via the natural entry point (writeStatic) is almost impossible for random fuzz: FS.stat gates writeDir behind on-disk directory existence, so the fuzzer cannot drive request.url for the regex. The practical pattern is to extract the module-local function (`Module._compile` with an appended export) and feed it directly, as attempts 4-5 do. For dense taint-chain findings a similar module-rewrite trick will often be the only way to actually exercise the sink.

4. Attempt 3 is a cautionary tale about overlapping detectors in the same file: the fuzzer landed a legitimate Path Traversal hit at lib/static.js:10 (Path.join with '../../jaz_zer' after fs.stat was stubbed) long before the regex at line 55 could be exercised. If a file carries findings for several classes, a harness that passes the Jazzer-plant sentinel sites unprotected will confirm the first available detector — which may be the wrong one for the finding you are targeting.
